doc.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

chapter: Cello group, family and the road
title: Finding babysitters on the road, including Hawaii
summary: Hiring child-minders in different cities and the Hawaii incident where their daughter wandered to the lobby; first child in 1952.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: What would happen if you have a duo gig, and you’re on the road in your station wagon, what did you do with your child while you were performing?

Well we went to Hawaii, and we were working at this hotel on the roof, and we got into there and didn’t know who we were going get, and finally we found a young Japanese girl who was very responsible, and we would get ready for work and she would come in and read to our first daughter, and then put her to bed, and this Japanese girl would go into the bathroom with the lights on, and do her reading and do her homework, and take care that we finish our show, and we’d come in and she’d go home.

We had to find people wherever we were and it was always very nerve wracking because you know, are we going to find somebody for the first night? And in fact, in that incident, in Hawaii, we didn’t have anyone for the first night, but luckily it was in the same hotel, and so we got her to sleep and we went upstairs and did our show, but this is what happened. She heard us. She woke up and she heard us because it was all open, there was no air conditioning, it was like an open roof thing, and it was just screened in. And in fact I don’t even know if it was screened in. But anyway she heard us and she went out of the room in her little Dr. Denton’s and she went looking for us, and ended up down in the lobby and the people in the lobby said well where are your parents, little girl? And she said well I hear them singing. And so somebody took over. But that was — the only reason she could get out is because the door was one of those that you lock with a little button on the inside, and so she could open it from the inside but you couldn’t get in from the outside. So anyway that was one of the funny incidents. And a lot of stuff like that happened. But most of the time we were very good, I mean we were lucky we found people the first day we got there through somebody in the club who knew somebody or whatever it was. And then eventually when we had our second child, we started carrying a live-in woman, a mother’s au pair, like a mother’s helper. And that was good because we had somebody steady then who went with us. Well we couldn’t that until we made a little more money so we could afford to pay her. But we were lucky in that sense.
When was your next chance to record, at this point? I’m sorry, this was around mid-50’s?
First child in ‘52, so we played and performed everywhere.
I think that’s when we did the last big band.
